articles.title: 10 Children, 9 Home Births: How ASHA Workers Changed the Fate of a High-Risk Delivery in Damoh
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Kusum Adivasi (38), a resident of Raneh village in the Hata block of Damoh district, has given birth to her tenth child. Both the mother and the newborn are healthy.

body.html:
Kusum Adivasi (38), a resident of Raneh village in the Hata block of Damoh district, has given birth to her tenth child. Both the mother and the newborn are healthy. The delivery took place at the Raneh Primary Health Centre (PHC) after health workers identified the pregnancy as high-risk.

According to health officials, Kusum had delivered her previous nine children at home. However, due to complications including anaemia and the risks associated with repeated home deliveries, ASHA workers advised institutional delivery. Acting on their recommendation, Kusum was admitted to the PHC, where she had a normal delivery on Thursday. The baby boy weighs 3.5 kg and is healthy.

Kusum’s husband, Nandram (43), a labourer, said the couple has been married for about 18 years. Their eldest child is 17 years old. The family now has three sons and seven daughters. Nandram stated that after the birth of their tenth child, they have decided not to have more children and have agreed to undergo a sterilisation procedure.

Devaki Kurmi, the nurse who conducted the delivery, said Kusum was categorised as a high-risk case. “She was brought to the hospital by an ASHA worker. Despite the risks, the delivery was normal, and both mother and child are completely safe,” she said.

Health officials said Kusum was initially reluctant to deliver at a hospital due to long-standing rural practices and a preference for home births. ASHA supervisor Kunti Chaurasia, along with ANM Kunti Chaurasia and ASHA worker Rajbai Lodhi, visited Kusum’s home regularly for nine months. They conducted health check-ups, provided nutritional guidance, explained the risks of home delivery, and reassured her about the safety of government health facilities.

Kusum said that without the repeated efforts of ASHA workers, she would have delivered at home again. “I now understand the benefits of hospital delivery. It ensured the safety of both me and my child,” she said, expressing gratitude to the health staff.

ASHA supervisor Kunti Chaurasia confirmed that convincing Kusum was challenging. “Her tenth pregnancy was risky, and she was not ready to come to the hospital. Continuous counselling helped, and finally she agreed. The delivery at Raneh PHC was safe,” she said.

articles.title: Anganwadi Worker Murdered in Varanasi, Accused Couple Nabbed After CCTV Shoe Clue
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Varanasi: Police have arrested a young couple in connection with the brutal murder of a 45-year-old Anganwadi worker whose blood-soaked body was found inside her house in the Shivpur police station area of Varanasi on December 11.

body.html:
Varanasi: Police have arrested a young couple in connection with the brutal murder of a 45-year-old Anganwadi worker whose blood-soaked body was found inside her house in the Shivpur police station area of Varanasi on December 11. The accused have been identified as Mohit Yadav (21) and his wife Anjali Chauhan (21).

The victim, Anupama alias Sita, was found dead in a locked room at her residence in Lachhimanpur, Shivpur. She had suffered severe head injuries and her throat had been slit. A grinding stone and sharp objects were allegedly used in the crime.

According to police, the accused confessed that Mohit had been in a relationship with the Anganwadi worker for several years. He alleged that the woman was pressuring him for sexual relations and even offered money, while threatening to implicate him in a police case if he refused. Mohit claimed he shared his distress with his wife, following which the couple planned the murder.

ADCP Neetu Kadyan said Mohit lived on rent near the victim’s house and met her while buying milk. A year ago, Mohit married Anjali, which the Anganwadi worker reportedly opposed. After the marriage, Mohit and Anjali shifted elsewhere, but the woman allegedly continued to threaten him.

On the morning of December 11, when the victim’s husband Shailesh Kumar Patel had left home at around 5 am to sell milk, the accused reached the house. Police said Anjali knocked on the door on the pretext of buying curd, after which Mohit entered the house. The accused slit the woman’s throat from behind and smashed her head with a grinding stone to make the murder appear like a robbery. They fled with jewellery worth about ₹2 lakh and ₹73,640 in cash.

The victim’s husband returned around 10 am to find the door open and his wife missing. On opening a locked room, he found her body lying in a pool of blood. Neighbours alerted the police, following which forensic teams collected evidence from the spot.

During the investigation, police scanned over 200 CCTV cameras. The couple was identified through CCTV footage and shoe impressions found at the crime scene. The accused were arrested near Shivpur railway station while allegedly trying to flee. Blood-stained clothes, the murder weapons, stolen jewellery and cash were recovered on their disclosure.

Police said the accused had even taken photographs of the victim after the murder, leaving their mobile phone behind at the scene. The victim, who was posted at the Khajuri Anganwadi centre and also worked as a BLO, had been married for over a decade and had no children.

A murder case has been registered, and further legal proceedings are underway. The Police Commissioner has announced a reward of ₹50,000 for the team involved in cracking the case.

articles.title: Fake OTT Subscriptions Scam Busted: Six Arrested for Cheating NRIs with Pirated Content
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Police have arrested six people for allegedly cheating NRIs living abroad by offering fake subscriptions to Indian, Pakistani and other international OTT platforms at discounted rates. The accused copied original OTT content and sold illegal subscriptions through online platforms.

body.html:
Police have arrested six people for allegedly cheating NRIs living abroad by offering fake subscriptions to Indian, Pakistani and other international OTT platforms at discounted rates. The accused copied original OTT content and sold illegal subscriptions through online platforms.

According to the police, the gang charged between $100 and $300 per subscription. In many cases, the subscriptions were terminated after a short period, following which victims were repeatedly asked to pay money for reactivation.

The accused were operating under the name “Web Biz Service LLC” from the Phase 1 police station area. Using internet calls, they contacted NRIs and provided them with fake OTT channels and unauthorised subscriptions.

The arrested accused have been identified as Tanishka, Anil Baghel, Manish Kumar Tripathi, Gaurav, Radha Ballabh and Yogesh Baghel, all aged between 20 and 30 years.

During the raid, police recovered 20 mobile phones, five CPUs, five computer monitors, one laptop, six keyboards and other electronic equipment.

Investigations revealed that pirated content from platforms such as Netflix, Disney+ Hotstar, Amazon Prime Video, Zee5, Voot Select, Sony LIV, ALTBalaji, MX Player, JioCinema, HBO and Hulu, along with recent movie releases, was illegally captured and rebroadcast without any licence.

Further investigation in the case is underway.

articles.title: : Shopkeeper Slapped for Filming Police, But His Own 75 Viral Videos Expose Guns
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A high-voltage controversy has erupted in Kanpur after a shopkeeper accused a police officer of assault and misconduct. However, a subsequent inquiry revealed that the complainant and his father have a significant criminal history, including previous clashes with police personnel.

body.html:
A high-voltage controversy has erupted in Kanpur after a shopkeeper accused a police officer of assault and misconduct. However, a subsequent inquiry revealed that the complainant and his father have a significant criminal history, including previous clashes with police personnel.

On 6 December, Kalyanpur Panki Road outpost in-charge Pushpraj was conducting vehicle checking with his team near the Kalyanpur railway crossing. During the operation, a bike was found parked outside a shop and was seized for further inquiry. At this point, a young man standing outside the shop began recording the checking on his mobile phone.

The officer objected, telling him not to interfere in government work. When he refused, the officer slapped him and confiscated his mobile phone to delete the video. The youth identified himself as Abhay Pratap alias Vikas, a cosmetics shopowner from Panki Road Galla Mandi.

While accessing the phone, the officer reportedly found around 75 videos, including clips of Abhay firing a pistol, consuming alcohol with friends inside a coaching class, and taking part in a half-naked bike parade on a highway. Shortly after, Abhay and his father Ashish reached the outpost and accused the officer of snatching Rs 15,000.

Inspector Pushpraj stated that he slapped Abhay because he abused him. He also submitted the recovered videos and lodged a separate complaint, citing the youth’s criminal record.

Police records confirmed that Abhay and his father have been involved in earlier offences. On 3 July, Abhay allegedly misbehaved with Constable Janam Singh during a traffic jam clearance near Kalyanpur crossing. He was later sent to jail in that case. On the same day, his father Ashish allegedly recorded videos at the spot, introduced himself as a journalist at the police station, and sought Rs 50,000. When refused, he made the video viral.

Another extortion complaint was filed on 5 July by Dheeraj Singh of Kalyanpur Kalan, alleging that Ashish demanded Rs 30,000 over a property-related dispute and chased him with a stick when he resisted.

After Abhay lodged a complaint with the Police Commissioner on 10 December and the video of the slap went viral, Inspector Pushpraj was placed under suspension. ADCP West Kapil Dev Singh confirmed that the father-son duo have a history of assaulting a constable and said that an FIR is being registered on the officer’s complaint.

articles.title: Student Molested in Broad Daylight in Hathras District
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A disturbing incident of public harassment occurred in the Sikandrarao area of Hathras district, Uttar Pradesh, when two female students returning from coaching classes were molested by men on a motorcycle. The assault took place around 5:00 PM in the Naurangabad West neighborhood.

body.html:
A disturbing incident of public harassment occurred in the Sikandrarao area of Hathras district, Uttar Pradesh, when two female students returning from coaching classes were molested by men on a motorcycle.

The assault took place around 5:00 PM in the Naurangabad West neighborhood. Two men riding a motorcycle approached the students, inappropriately touched their faces, and quickly fled the scene. The entire incident was recorded by nearby CCTV cameras, and the footage has since spread widely across social media platforms.

Local residents have voiced serious concerns about the growing frequency of such incidents. Community members report that female students face regular harassment from perpetrators who appear undeterred by law enforcement presence. The brazen nature of this attack, occurring in broad daylight in a public area, has particularly alarmed residents.

These incidents persist despite the Uttar Pradesh government's Mission Shakti campaign, an initiative designed to protect women and girls from violence and harassment.

Law enforcement authorities have responded to the incident with urgency. Based on the CCTV evidence, police have identified the suspects and arrested one accused individual, Ankush, son of Naresh Chandra Upadhyay. Officials have assured the public that they will identify the second perpetrator shortly and that legal proceedings against both individuals are currently underway.

The case highlights ongoing challenges in ensuring women's safety in public spaces, even with increased awareness campaigns and governmental initiatives in place.

articles.title: Purvanchal Expressway Horror: Constable’s Entire Family Burned Alive as SUV Overruns Parked Car
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A devastating road accident on the Purvanchal Expressway in Barabanki, Uttar Pradesh, claimed five members of a policeman’s family on 10 December 2025. The deceased included the wife and four children of Azamgarh constable Javed Ashraf Siddiqui.

body.html:
A devastating road accident on the Purvanchal Expressway in Barabanki, Uttar Pradesh, claimed five members of a policeman’s family on 10 December 2025. The deceased included the wife and four children of Azamgarh constable Javed Ashraf Siddiqui.

The incident occurred around 4 PM near Dih village in the Haidergarh area when a speeding Maruti Brezza SUV crashed into the family’s parked WagonR. The impact was so severe that bodies were flung nearly 20 metres, and both vehicles were engulfed in flames. The WagonR’s doors were locked, trapping the occupants as the fire spread rapidly, reportedly fuelled by a suspected CNG cylinder explosion.

Passersby managed to pull out some of the injured before fire teams reached the spot. The blaze led to significant traffic congestion on the expressway.

Constable Siddiqui’s wife, Chandni alias Gulfshan (30), and their four children—daughters Samreen (reported as 22), Ilma (10), Isma (8), and son Zian (10)—died on the spot, many of them burned alive. Chandni’s brother, Zeeshan, who was driving the WagonR, survived with serious injuries and is undergoing treatment in Lucknow. Three occupants of the Brezza were also injured, one of them critically. A total of five injured individuals from both vehicles were initially treated at local hospitals before being referred further.

Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath extended condolences and directed officials to provide relief and ensure proper medical care for the survivors. Police suspect the Brezza driver may have dozed off at the wheel. The investigation is underway, including why the WagonR was parked on the expressway and the source of the fire.

The family was travelling from Azamgarh to Lucknow and had reportedly stopped briefly to drink water.

articles.title: Female Teacher Caught With Senior Colleague in Oyo Hotel; Husband Creates Ruckus, Police Detain Both
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking incident in Uttar Pradesh has brought disgrace to the education fraternity. On Wednesday evening, a female teacher was caught red-handed by her husband inside an Oyo hotel room with a senior teacher from the same institution.

body.html:
A shocking incident in Uttar Pradesh has brought disgrace to the education fraternity. On Wednesday evening, a female teacher was caught red-handed by her husband inside an Oyo hotel room with a senior teacher from the same institution. The confrontation quickly turned chaotic, drawing a large crowd and forcing the police to intervene.

According to reports, the husband barged into the hotel room, where he allegedly found his wife and the senior teacher together. Enraged, he pulled her out on the road and assaulted her, leading to a public uproar. Hotel staff immediately informed the police, who arrived at the spot without delay.

Police detained both the female teacher and her senior colleague for questioning. The hotel staff, registers, and CCTV footage are now under scrutiny to determine how the teachers checked in and the circumstances surrounding the incident. Officials have confirmed that a detailed report will also be forwarded to the Education Department for further action.

Meanwhile, videos of the confrontation are circulating widely on social media, fuelling discussions and shock across the district.

articles.title: Lizard Found in Zomato-Delivered Chicken in Meerut; Youth Hospitalised, FIR Filed
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A disturbing incident has emerged from Meerut, where a dead lizard was found in chicken ordered through the Zomato app. The youth who consumed the food, identified as Neeraj, works for a private company in Ghaziabad.

body.html:
A disturbing incident has emerged from Meerut, where a dead lizard was found in chicken ordered through the Zomato app. The youth who consumed the food, identified as Neeraj, works for a private company in Ghaziabad.

According to Neeraj, he was staying at his friend Vijay’s house on December 8. As it was late, Vijay ordered kadhai chicken from Ananta Hospitality’s ‘Kakke Da Hotel’ via Zomato. After serving the food in separate bowls, Vijay went to wash his hands. Neeraj began eating and was halfway through the meal when he noticed a dead lizard in the chicken. Shocked, he immediately began vomiting, and his condition deteriorated quickly.

A panicked Vijay dialed 112. Police reached the spot and rushed Neeraj to a medical college. He remained under medical supervision for nearly 24 hours and was discharged the next day, December 9.

After being discharged, Neeraj filed a complaint at the Medical Police Station against the owner of Ananta Hospitality’s Kakke Da Hotel. He stated that such negligence endangers public health and strict action must be taken. Inspector Shiv Prakash Singh confirmed that a complaint has been received and an investigation is underway. The Food Department has also been informed.
